newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westpac diversifies funding with Euro-MTN.
newsitem.headline: Westpac diversifies funding with Euro-MTN.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corporation said its US$5.0 billion Euro Medium Term Note programme announced on Monday will allow a broad base of funding globally and is a key element of Westpac's Treasury management.

"The Euro Medium Term Note Programe programme provides diversification of funding source by investor type, geographical location, term, currency and structure," said Marten Touw, Westpac's Group Treasurer.
"It will also reduce the volatility and cost of the bank's wholesale funding base and is a logical step in our global funding strategy," Touw said in a statement.
Touw believes that European monetary union will lead investors to focus on the credit quality of issuers.
"Westpac's existing profile in the Euro-markets and its strong credit rating will provide a sound platform for achieving further funding diversification within this changing environment," Touw said.
Senior debt issuance under the programme is rated Aa3 by Moody's Investors Service and AA minus by Standard & Poor's.
Touw said that Westpac has established a sound reputation as a strategic issuer in the Euro debt markets with six publicly syndicated floating rate notes since October 1995.
Westpac would continue to access the public markets on a strategic basis as funding opportunities arise.

"We also intend to use the new programme to access other sectors of the public markets, particularly for fixed rate and retail targeted transactions, as well as opportunistic private placements," Touw added.

Morgan Stanley arranged the programme and the dealer group comprises Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, HSBC Markets, J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley International, Nomura International, Westpac Banking Corporation and SBC Warburg. The fiscal agent is the Chase Manhattan Bank. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
